item.title: Why 1 final celebration meant ‘a lot’ to Knicks’ Karl-Anthony Towns before Opening Night vs. 76ers
item.description: Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Why 1 final celebration meant ‘a lot’ to Knicks’ Karl-Anthony Towns before Opening Night vs. 76ers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Knicks reaped the rewards of last season’s hard work prior to their season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers. Not only did they receive their championship rings, they also saw championship banner number three get lifted towards the rafters at Madison Square Garden. The fans in attendance at Madison Square Garden showered the reigning champions with so much praise, and Karl-Anthony Towns certainly felt like he was living the dream. Of course, nothing in the NBA is permanent. A new season has just begun, and the championship is going to be up for grabs once more. Suffice to say, the Knicks’ perch at the top of the NBA mountain is only temporary. But Towns was thankful for the opportunity to bask in the fans’ adoration one more time before facing reality — especially after suffering a 106-100 loss to the 76ers to start the new campaign. “To celebrate one last time with the fans, it means a lot. We wanted to give them a better version of ourselves tonight than we did, but it was really special to have that moment here again in New York after 53 years,” Towns told reporters, via SNY Knicks on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "To celebrate one last time with the fans, it means a lot. We wanted to give them a better version of ourselves tonight than we did, but it was really special to have that moment here again in New York after 53 years." – Karl-Anthony Towns pic.twitter.com/vv69pVBK1X — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 21, 2026 Towns, to his credit, was one of the few Knicks players who put up a fight in the fourth quarter. He made two huge threes that kept the Knicks within striking distance late in the fourth, which helped make up for the fact that he was limited to just 23 minutes on the night after getting into foul trouble early. He finished with 19 points and 12 boards on the night. The Knicks hold themselves to a higher standard than what they showed on Tuesday, and it looked like they were suffering from championship hangover. They will now be looking to redeem themselves on Friday in a contest on the road against the Boston Celtics. item.title: Braylon Mullins injury puts damper on UConn basketball’s 2026-27 outlook
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Braylon Mullins injury puts damper on UConn basketball’s 2026-27 outlook appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In less than two weeks, No. 4-ranked UConn basketball will begin its 2026-27 season with a showdown against the Gardner-Webb Runnin’ Bulldogs at PeoplesBank Arena in Hartford, but there seems to be uncertainty with regard to the status of sophomore guard Braylon Mullins after he didn’t play in Tuesday’s exhibition game against the No. 6-ranked Michigan State Spartans down at Breslin Center in East Lansing. “Sources: UConn’s Braylon Mullins (undisclosed) went through shootaround and part of warmups, but is not expected to play in tonight’s exhibition game against Michigan State. DNP in last week’s exhibition game against Syracuse. Averaged 12.0 PPG last season,” Jon Rothstein of CBS Sports shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter. Despite playing Mullins, UConn basketball managed to beat the Spartans, 78-70. Nik Khamenia led the way for the Huskies with 19 points, while Silas Demary Jr. and Colben Landrew racked up 16 and 13 points, respectively. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) UConn also leaned on the long ball to thwart the host team, with the Huskies torching the Spartans with 10-for-25 shooting from behind the arc, while also dishing out 21 assists on 27 field goals. Speaking of 3-pointers, Mullins is perhaps best known to date for his stunning 3-pointer to help UConn basketball beat and eliminate the Duke Blue Devils in the 2026 edition of March Madness. During his freshman season in 2025-26, Mullins averaged 12.0 points on 42.1 percent shooting from the floor and 33.5 percent from deep, 3.5 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 33 games, including 29 starts. The Huskies should be able to take care of business against Gardner-Webb with or without Mullins, but the game after that will be a big test early in the seaosn for UConn, with the Michigan Wolverines challenging Dan Hurley’s squad in a neutral-site game on Nov. 6. item.title: 76ers superstar LeBron James shares special handshake with VJ Edgecombe after first Philly win
item.description: Kyle Ross-Imagn Images. 76ers superstar LeBron James shares special handshake with VJ Edgecombe after first Philly win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Philadelphia 76ers superstar LeBron James shared a special postgame handshake with VJ Edgecombe after helping his new team defeat the defending NBA champion New York Knicks 106-100 on Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden. James, beginning his 24th NBA season and first with the 76ers , celebrated alongside the second-year guard after the Sixers spoiled New York’s championship festivities in their season opener. The Cashing Daily’s Max Jacobson took to X, formerly Twitter, to share footage of the four-time NBA MVP and Edgecombe interacting on the court following Philadelphia’s impressive road victory. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The footage showed James wearing his blue No. 23 jersey alongside Edgecombe, sporting No. 77, as cameras surrounded the teammates. Jacobson suggested James was taking the young guard under his wing as the Sixers began their new campaign with a victory. Looks like LeBron James Sr. has taken V. J. Edgecombe under his wing after beating the reigning NBA Champs and has quickly forgotten former teammate Lebron James Jr. who he previously had under his wing in LA pic.twitter.com/G2V4rsFHfR — Max (@FantasyFBallAZ) October 21, 2026 James finished his Philadelphia debut with 14 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, contributing across the board as the Sixers opened the 2026-27 season with a victory over their Atlantic Division rivals. Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers in scoring with 28 points, while Jaylen Brown added 19 points and eight rebounds in his first regular-season appearance with the franchise. Joel Embiid contributed 13 points and 11 rebounds, while Edgecombe finished with nine points and four rebounds. The Knicks entered Tuesday’s matchup celebrating their NBA championship, receiving their rings and raising their title banner before tipoff at Madison Square Garden. However, Philadelphia spoiled New York’s celebration behind a strong second-half performance. The Sixers used an 11-0 run to close the third quarter and eventually held off the Knicks’ late comeback attempt. James’ arrival and Brown’s addition have significantly reshaped Philadelphia’s roster, joining Maxey, Embiid, and the second-year standout from Baylor. The postgame interaction highlighted James and Edgecombe celebrating their first regular-season victory together, providing a memorable moment after Philadelphia’s season-opening win. item.title: Quiet Victor Wembanyama Opening Night 1st half vs. Thunder has Spurs fans worried
item.description: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Quiet Victor Wembanyama Opening Night 1st half vs. Thunder has Spurs fans worried appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It’s the start of the 2026-27 NBA Season, and San Antonio Spurs fans are starting to get worried. They are currently facing off against their new rivals, the Oklahoma City Thunder. What makes fans worried isn’t exactly the score, but the performance of their biggest weapon. Victor Wembanyama is expected to take a big leap after a breakout sophomore season, but his third year in the league is off to a rough start. At halftime, Wembanyama has just eight points. What’s even more brutal is that Wembanyama did not make a single field goal in the first half, missing all seven of his attempts from the field. He’s also a -11 when he’s on the floor, an uncharacteristic performance from the Spurs’ star center. Victor Wembanyama in the first half: Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) ❄️ 8 points ❄️ 0-of-7 shooting ❄️ 0-of-1 3PT ❄️ -11 Spurs trail by 21 points at halftime. pic.twitter.com/J1lHT61f1s — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 21, 2026 This development has brought a ton of stress among Spurs fans, who were expecting big things from Wembanyama this season. One fan pointed out that the Thunder might have figured out how to defend the center, and that his unwillingness to punish OKC is hurting the team. “Really don’t see what Victor Wembanyama did to improve his offensive game in the offseason. He seems more guardable as people adjust to what he can do and is not yet willing to do with the ball,” the fan noted. A French fan expressed frustration about how the Spurs were utilizing Wembanyama. His comment , translated to English, reads, “Wemby’s performance with the WCF was monstrous, he was putting up posters on you, dunks, insane alley-oops, so why’d we go back to that old offensive system making him play like he’s a point guard???” Another fan simply said that Wembanyama needed to show that he’s a star in the second half . “Victor Wembanyama has to be better. That was a flat out disgusting half.” At the time of writing, the Thunder lead the Spurs 80-70 midway through the third quarter. item.title: 'I'm going in the right direction' - Phil Foden hungry for more goals after starring with treble in Manchester City's 5-1 win over AEK Athens
item.description: Manchester City v AEK Athens - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport English playmaker inspires Etihad rout Foden is determined to keep building his goal tally after registering a treble and an assist during the Citizens' 150th Champions League fixture . Having been sent off in last month's Manchester derby before ending a scoring drought dating back to December at the weekend, he now boasts four goals in four days. Victory also provided the ideal response to last week's 4-2 home defeat against holders Paris Saint-Germain . Tactical switch unlocks clinical display Tactical switch unlocks clinical display The hosts opened the scoring when Elliot Anderson poked home his first goal for the club after fellow summer signing Enzo Fernandez clipped a free-kick against the crossbar, before Foden converted Rico Lewis' pass. Seven minutes after the restart, Stavros Pilios netted the first goal City had ever conceded against Greek opposition following four previous clean sheets against Aris and Olympiacos, only for Foden to tee up Rayan Cherki and add two further strikes . Expressing his delight with the collective performance while naming his second strike into the top corner as his favourite in a post-match interview with the club's official website , Foden said: "I enjoyed that a lot. The lads were great again. We showed determination again, it wasn't pretty at times. We were giving sloppy passes away. But, we stuck at the game plan and we kept going and in the end we broke them down. Overall I'm delighted. "[My favourite goal is] probably the second to be honest. The way it went in. I'm delighted to score goals now, I'm a forward so I have to keep scoring and helping the team. It'll only do good for my confidence." Reflecting on his bid to recapture peak form following two indifferent seasons and his enjoyment of a central attacking role, he continued: "Slowly but surely [getting back to my best], still got a long way to go. item.title: UConn's Braylon Mullins sits out second exhibition, but should be ready for Purdue next week
item.description: UConn's Solo Ball and Braylon Mullins watch the team warm up before the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame Exhibition Series preseason game against Syracuse at Mohegan Sun Arena in Uncasville, Conn., Tuesday, October 13, 2026. (Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) EAST LANSING, Mich. - Dan Hurley considered playing Braylon Mullins in the first half of the UConn men's basketball team's exhibition bout with Michigan State on Tuesday night. Mullins, out for nearly a month with an undisclosed injury, had practiced for three straight days and appeared just about ready to make his 2026-27 debut. He participated in pregame warm-ups, but by the time the Huskies returned to the floor for their final warm-ups prior to the opening tap, Mullins was in civilian clothes alongside fellow injured shooter Solo Ball. "We shut him down," Hurley said of Mullins. "We should have him ready for Purdue, as long as there's no setbacks." UConn hosts Purdue on Oct. 27 at PeoplesBank Arena in its final exhibition tune-up. Hurley feels it's important for Mullins, a Big East All-Freshman team pick last season after averaging 12 points per game, to get in at least one exhibition before the games start to count on Nov. 2 in Hartford against Gardner-Webb. "Obviously, we've got to protect a player's health," Hurley said. "But, these are excellent reps to get right now." UConn's offense looked very sharp in Tuesday night's 78-70 win over Sparty at Breslin Center, even without Mullins. "Braylon is such a prolific player," Hurley explained, "him not being available forced us to cut better, work on execution and our shuffles and twirls, the things we do to put pressure on the rim without ball screen and roll or post-up." item.title: Dan Hurley, Tom Izzo relationship sparked by NBA interest in UConn men's basketball coach
item.description: EAST LANSING, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: (L-R) Head coach Tom Izzo of the Michigan State Spartans talks to head coach Dan Hurley of the UConn Huskies before the start of the game at Breslin Center. (Rey Del Rio/Getty Images) Dan Hurley returned to the college basketball mountaintop in the summer of 2024 and considered climbing higher, faced with a six-year, $70 million offer to coach the Los Angeles Lakers. Few people could relate to the UConn men's basketball coach's predicament, so he built a relationship with Michigan State coach Tom Izzo, the seventh-winningest active coach in Division I basketball, who had received multiple NBA offers over his long run with the Spartans. Hurley chose to stay in the college game, and he's quickly formed a friendship with Izzo, bringing his UConn program to East Lansing for an exhibition game Tuesday evening . "Danny and I talked a year ago, we went out there and played," Izzo said on the Big Ten Network broadcast Tuesday. "He's been a good friend of mine. He had some NBA offers, I went through it a little bit myself, we just talked about it and we just became good friends. I love what he does, I love what he stands for, and I knew playing them, they'd be tough as nails." Izzo began his legendary coaching career at Michigan State in 1995 while Hurley played his senior season at Seton Hall. Inheriting a program that had not reached the Final Four since Magic Johnson, Izzo needed just five seasons to bring a title to East Lansing, winning the 2000 national championship with a talented roster that included Jason Richardson and Morris Peterson. Izzo was offered the Atlanta Hawks head coaching job that summer, which he rejected, and over a quarter-century later the legendary tactician continues to draw professional interest - Izzo said he spoke seriously with Phoenix Suns owner and former Spartan player Mat Ishbia about coaching the team. Hurley is a relative newcomer to the coaching scene, but he's adopted an old-school approach that more closely resembles Izzo's, so much so that both men are in an "old-school coaches" group chat alongside Thatta Matta and Mick Cronin. Izzo and Hurley have publicly aligned on player eligibility and transfer portal regulation, and their two programs also played an exhibition game in Connecticut to kick off last season. "They buried us out there last year," Izzo said. "It was a 15-point game, but they dominated the game. He said to me after, 'You've got a ways to go.' At least you can be honest with some coaches." Izzo's Spartans were more competitive on home soil Tuesday evening, led by a standout 23-point, eight-rebound effort from Spartans point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. However, the Huskies worked past early free-throw woes down the stretch and salted away a comfortable 78-70 win. item.title: Bryce Underwood's Michigan future bleak after Kyle Whittingham's call before Indiana game
item.description: Bryce Underwood's Michigan future bleak after Kyle Whittingham's call before Indiana game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Michigan Wolverines didn't waste any time regarding which quarterback will start Saturday when they host the Indiana Hoosiers on Big Noon Kickoff (noon ET, FOX) in Ann Arbor. Although the Wolverines beat Penn State 21-18 last week, quarterback Bryce Underwood was benched after throwing two interceptions and completing only 5 of 11 pass attempts for 43 yards. In a relief effort, Tommy Carr replaced Underwood. Although Carr, a freshman quarterback who had previously appeared in a 52-17 win against UTEP, threw only two passes, the limited sample size was enough for the Wolverines to make a change with a little over a month left in the regular season. According to On3's Pete Nakos, Carr will get his first career start. It's unclear whether this move will remain permanent, but given coach Kyle Whittingham's previous uncertainty surrounding Underwood, it's apparent that the move was going to happen sooner rather than later. "Well, he only had about 70 yards or thereabouts in the first half, and no points, and we just needed to get something done and create a spark, as we said," Whittingham said after the win when asked about Underwood. MORE: College Football Playoff bracket for Week 8: Projecting top four seeds, first-round matchups, bubble teams The plan seemed to work, as the Wolverines took control in the second half to snap their two-game losing streak. "He's always prepared. I walk by the quarterback room 12 times, 15 times a day," Whittingham said of Carr's dedication. "He's in there pretty much every second he doesn't have class, he's in there watching film. So, he's very prepared when his number was called. Like I said, he responded very well. Going forward, we'll take a good, hard look at the tape and see why things bogged down in the first half and why we were a little better in the second half, because there really wasn't a lot of scheme change." During his Monday presser, Whittingham wasn't prepared to name Carr as the Week 8 quarterback. Now that it's reportedly official, it raises more questions about where the Wolverines' season goes from here. MORE: College football picks, predictions against the spread for Week 8 matchups Regardless of who the quarterback is, however, ESPN's Kirk Herbstreit said Whittingham could be on thin ice when it comes to his job security should he be unable to fix the current struggles Michigan is facing. "And I know by doing that, if it doesn't work out, you know, you probably get fired, Herbstreit said on the "Nonstop" podcast. So, in a nutshell, transitioning to Carr may be a last-ditch effort to save the Wolverines' season. The question remains, however: will it? As Saturday approaches, we'll have our answer soon. item.title: Detroit's J.B. Bickerstaff sends bold message on 'Pistons basketball' after win over Celtics
item.description: Detroit's J.B. Bickerstaff sends bold message on 'Pistons basketball' after win over Celtics originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Pistons pulled off a comeback win for their opening game of the NBA's regular season, and it really couldn't have been more dramatic. The team came from behind to win this matchup in a 121-113 victory . The Pistons' stars were obviously on the court, including Cade Cunningham and Jalen Duren, the latter of whom just inked a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract with the team. After the game, Pistons head coach J.B. Bickerstaff spoke to reporters about what this win meant to kick off Detroit's season. The Pistons' comeback win showed why Detroit's gritty identity could make the team tough to beat "The opponent doesn't matter. What people say doesn't matter," Bickerstaff said, according to ESPN . "The only thing that matters is if we play Pistons basketball. I thought tonight we found enough stretches where we did, and when we played Pistons basketball, we're hard to beat. That's the only thing that matters." While some Detroit fans perhaps would have preferred a win that didn't have them biting their nails up until the end, Duren told reporters that the team's big comeback "just embodied the culture and what we're trying to build here." He added, per ESPN, "We're a team that's known to be gritty, known to get it out the mud, known to never quit, and that's our identity. Even the guys who are new here are embodying that. And that's why we were able to have the outcome that we had." Before the game, Cunningham spoke to the Detroit crowd and thanked them for everything. "All my teammates, the entire Pistons organization wants to say thank you for all the love and support," he said. Next up, the Pistons head to Florida to take on the Miami Heat on Friday. The New York Knicks celebrated their first NBA ring ceremony in 53 years at Madison Square Garden before their 2026-27 season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers. Team owner James Dolan and the staff played an important role in organizing the celebration and making the occasion memorable. Hence, Knicks head coach Mike Brown extended his appreciation to Dolan. In the press conference, Brown made sure to recognize Dolan and the other members of the organization for their efforts in delivering a successful celebration. “I would like to give, and I don’t know who was behind it, but you know, obviously starting with Mr. Dolan and everybody else, you know, did a fantastic job with the ceremony. You know, okay, like you said, everybody, you know, you guys did a fantastic job; they weren’t mud like us, so thank you.” The Knicks’ ring ceremony was a dream come true for the franchise and its supporters, as the celebration honored the team’s first NBA championship since 1973. The players received their championship rings in front of a raucous Madison Square Garden crowd. Hall of Famer Walt Frazier, who played on the Knicks’ previous championship-winning teams in 1970 and 1973, presented the rings. His participation connected the franchise’s championship past with its latest success. The celebration also marked the beginning of a new challenge for New York. After spending the offseason enjoying its championship success, the Knicks had to shift their focus toward defending their title and proving that they could maintain their position among the NBA’s elite teams. However, Jalen Brunson’s team could not sustain its championship celebrations for long on Tuesday, as the 76ers handed the Knicks a 106-100 loss in their season opener. There are win-now seasons and then campaigns that have a bit less urgency, and right now, those three teams are looking for a way to put themselves over the top, something a running back with a 2,000-yard campaign on his resume can absolutely do. With the Eagles’ cap already in a tough spot heading into the future, finding a way to ship off more veterans on long-term contracts is an ideal way to use 2026, especially if teams believe they are shopping at a premium purveyor, instead of the outlets. item.title: Red Sox Still Owe Jordan Hicks $4 Million to Pitch for White Sox in 2027
item.description: The Boston Red Sox will still be paying $4 million to Jordan Hicks in 2027, even though he now pitches for the Chicago White Sox. Getty When the Boston Red Sox traded away their three-time All-Star slugger Rafael Devers on June 15, 2025, the headline of the multilayer package they received from the San Francisco Giants was 100-mph throwing right-handed reliever Jordan Hicks. But Hicks was such a disappointment that the Red Sox traded him to the Chicago White Sox in February, in what one analyst called “a clear salary dump from the Red Sox.” But even though the Red Sox were eager to free themselves from the money owed to Hicks, they are still paying him. In fact, Boston still owes Hicks $4 million in 2027, even though he will be in his second full season with the White Sox, where he reached the playoffs and helped Chicago advance to the American League Division Series this year. Boston committed $8 million in cash to Chicago in the Feb. 1 trade, a sum divided into $4 million for 2026 and $4 million for 2027, according to The Athletic. Pitching prospect David Sandlin went to Chicago in the same deal, and the Red Sox got another pitching prospect, Gage Ziehl, back, according to MassLive. Read More From Heavy Red Sox Gave Up on Pitcher From Devers Trade, Now He’s Going to the World Series Why the Boston Red Sox Still Owe Jordan Hicks Hicks arrived from the San Francisco Giants on June 15, 2025, in the Devers trade, carrying the four-year, $44 million contract he signed in January 2024. That deal pays him $12 million per season from 2025 through 2027, according to MLB.com . Chicago absorbed roughly $16 million of the $24 million left on the contract, leaving Boston with $4 million per season, including the 2027 payment still to be paid. The contract expires after 2027, and no other Boston-tied salary or bonus is reported, according to Spotrac . The trade cleared 2026 and 2027 commitments, pushed Boston under the second luxury-tax threshold and opened 40-man roster spots, according to The Athletic . Chicago had payroll room after trading Luis Robert Jr., and Sandlin served as the sweetener. Hicks arrived on the injured list with right toe inflammation, then went down again with right shoulder tendinitis, according to The Associated Press . He issued 12 walks against 97 batters faced, a 12.4% walk rate , well above the MLB average of 8.4%. Hicks finished 2025 with a 6.95 ERA across 34 games for San Francisco and Boston combined, his worst season in the majors. Shoulder tendinitis ended his year when he went on the injured list Sept. 4. The walks persisted in 2026. Hicks posted a 15.3% walk rate for Chicago, though he finished 3-2 with a 3.94 ERA in 53 games and struck out 64 batters in 48 innings

And the risk paid off for the Blue Raiders coach in a 26-23 victory against FIU (3-4, 1-2) on Oct. 20 in Miami. item.title: Mike Penders becomes Chelsea’s youngest ever Premier League goalkeeper; now set to beat Petr Čech’s record
item.description: LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 17: Mike Penders of Chelsea FC during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Everton and Chelsea FC at Hill Dickinson Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) | Getty Images It probably didn’t happen exactly how he might have imagined it, but young Mike Penders made his Premier League debut over the weekend when he replaced the stricken Emiliano Martínez in the second half of Chelsea’s game against Everton at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The veteran goalkeeper, two-time recipient of the Yashin Trophy, suffered a fractured jaw and had to be rushed to hospital. No pressure, kid! Penders did get a few extra minutes to warm up as Martínez received treatment, but he was thrown straight into the action as the home side tried to get back on level terms. Thankfully, the youngster managed to complete the job that Emi started and keep a rare clean sheet for the Blues — making a couple impressive plays in the process in commanding his area, but also fumbling the ball once and getting knocked over on a set piece once as well. That’s Premier League football for ya! Afterwards on social media, Penders called it a “very proud moment” to have made his Premier League debut (while also sending well-wishes to Martínez), while the official Chelsea website confirmed that the 21-year-old in fact became our youngest ever goalkeeper in the competition , beating Lenny Pidgeley 21-year-old record. In this household, Pidgeley’s famous for being the first player always released at the start of any Chelsea save in CM 01/02. In real life, he did get to play for the Blues a couple times before leaving in 2006, including on the final day of the 2004-05 season, when José Mourinho subbed him on for the final few minutes of our last match of the season. He’d retire some dozen years later, after a decent career in the lower leagues. Presumably, a slightly different fate awaits Penders, who’s now set to start our next game, against Spurs at the Bridge. No pressure, kid! In fact, barring any unforeseen drama, Penders is thus set to become our youngest ever starting goalkeeper in the Premier League, beating the record of none other that than Petr Čech, who was 22 years and 87 days old when he started against Manchester United on the first day of the aforementioned 2004-05 season. Penders will be almost exactly a year Čech’s junior at 21 years, 85 days on Saturday. Chelsea were not quite ready to hand the keys to Penders in the summer; now he has to step in anyway. Čech did not let go of his spot for ten years after his first start. No pressure, kid! View this post on Instagram

item.title: Wojo: Pistons go bonkers in 23-0 run, shoot past Celtics in opener
item.description: Detroit – The Pistons were down 22 and it was looking bleak. Cade Cunningham wasn’t getting to the basket easily and the Celtics were doing what they do, hitting 3s from every corner. Detroit’s big opening-day showcase needed a boost. It started where it always starts, with smothering defense. It continued where it often continues, with a varied array of contributors. By the time the Pistons had finished off a 23-0 run on a 3-pointer by Javonte Green in the fourth quarter, it looked and sounded like a wild playoff game. It also looked and sounded like a lot of games will in the suddenly stacked Eastern Conference this season. The Pistons flipped that deficit into a stirring triumph at Little Caesars Arena Tuesday, ripping past the Celtics 121-113 in front of a crowd that roared like it was May. No messages are sent or received in the first game, with lots of new-look teams figuring things out. But in this one, the Pistons eventually flexed their old-look strengths. More: Green, Robinson lead Pistons to season-opening win over Celtics “Yeah, that's what makes us a team,” said Jalen Duren, in his first regular-season game since a protracted offseason contract negotiation. “I think the comeback just embodied the culture and what we're trying to build here. We're a team known to be gritty, known to get into the mud, known to never quit, and that's our identity. Even the guys who are new here are embodying that.” For all the focus on Cunningham, rightly so, J.B. Bickerstaff is always hunting for the next guy up. Duren was paid handsomely to stay, and looked happily at home again, with 22 points and nine rebounds. But on a day when the NBA celebrated its one-name stars and power teams, the Pistons again stood out for their unique build. The league’s season-opening, three-game national-TV extravaganza featured the Sixers -Knicks and Spurs-Thunder at night. The Celtics came in as one of the favorites — along with the Knicks and Sixers — to supplant the Pistons as the top seed in the Eastern Conference. The Pistons had the honors of tipping it off with the matinee, and they had a few of their own one-name pieces. Boston brought in Paul George, trying to recapture his stardom, and a fully healthy star Jayson Tatum, who had the misfortune of running into the Pistons defensive menace. Tatum was held to 13 points on 6-for-23 shooting (0-for-7 on 3s). How did that happen? “Ausar Thompson,” Bickerstaff said. “That simple. You get him in one-on-one situations, you're gonna be in for a long night, no matter who you are.” Just for fun, Thompson, one of the league’s elite defenders, added 11 points, 11 rebounds and dropped in a short jumper as the shot clock expired to seal it with 41 seconds left. The Pistons’ 22-point comeback was the largest in an NBA opener in at least 28 years. You get him in one-on-one situations, you're gonna be in for a long night, no matter who you are.” Just for fun, Thompson, one of the league’s elite defenders, added 11 points, 11 rebounds and dropped in a short jumper as the shot clock expired to seal it with 41 seconds left. The Pistons’ 22-point comeback was the largest in an NBA opener in at least 28 years. More: How Cade Cunningham will benefit from Pistons improved floor spacing Of course we’ve seen it before, often multiple times in the same games. All those crazy comebacks – and meltdowns, too – in the playoffs against the Magic and Cavs need to be smoothed out if the Pistons are to grab another high seed in the playoffs. It will be much, much tougher in the East, with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown joining the Sixers and Joel Embiid. You also have the newly crowned Knicks and others – Cleveland, Toronto, Miami and even Indiana – duly fortified. The Pistons do need to evolve, which is why Trajan Langdon brought in shooters John Collins, Isaiah Joe and Taurean Prince, and hopes Thompson can develop a more-dynamic offensive game. And then in the opener, they found shooting help on their own roster. Duncan Robinson (21 points, 5-for-9 on 3s) and Green (19 points, 5-for-8 on 3s) provided the spark in the second half, when the Pistons outscored the Celtics 76-55. It was dazzling at times, as each hit clutch 3 after clutch 3, turning a noisy arena atmosphere into pandemonium. “We got a high level of trust in everybody on our roster,” Bickerstaff said. “Tonight, I thought we needed just a little bit of a boost, and Woo, time and time again, does it for us. He could have sat over there and been pissed off because he didn't play in the first half, but that's not the makeup of this group. I thought Duncan and Woo did a great job of catching that spark for us.” Wait a minute. Woo? Woo Who? “Nobody knows where the nickname came from,” Green said, smiling. “I'm sorry, but we've been asking the same question for six years now. Nobody knows. My mom doesn't know. My grandma doesn't know. Wish I had an answer for you.” Green certainly had an answer for Bickerstaff, who saw his team getting blistered by the Celtics’ deep shooting. The Pistons won’t ever be as 3-heavy as Boston, but they are trying to space the floor to help Cunningham create better shots. By the end of this one, the Pistons (15-for-40 on 3s) and Celtics (17-for-42) had nearly identical shooting stats. Who knew it would start with a guy that didn’t play a second in the first half. But Woo knew what was needed. “I guess we were lacking energy,” said Green, who averaged 6.9 points while playing in all 82 games for the Pistons last season. “We weren't playing as hard as we know we can play on the defensive end. We play our way, everything else will fall in place. In the first half, and probably the beginning of the third quarter, we weren't playing Detroit basketball.” Detroit basketball is back, with a largely unchanged foundation and a significantly bigger challenge. Winning 60 games again seems improbable. Can the Pistons’ shooting catch up, or keep up, with the East’s glitterati? For a Tuesday matinee, it was an entertaining show against one of those marquee opponents. Cunningham had said he felt the Pistons were being “slept on,” overlooked in preseason prognostications. The team alternately claims it doesn’t care, then relishes the edge it brings. “The opponent doesn't matter,” Bickerstaff. “What people say doesn't matter. The only thing that matters is if we play Pistons basketball. And when we play Pistons basketball, we're hard to beat.” And when they shoot like this? Woo-wee, they’re really hard to beat. item.title: PETA urges Crystal Palace to 'let Phoenix spread his wings' and permanently retire live bald eagle mascot from matchday duties
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-CRYSTAL PALACE-MAN CITY - AFP Animal welfare group demands change Animal rights group PETA has demanded that the Eagles hierarchy permanently halt the use of their live bald eagle, Phoenix, during matchday build-ups. In a formal letter sent to club CEO Sharon Lacey, the organisation called on officials to commit to "never using a live animal mascot again". Sourced from the Eagle Heights Wildlife Foundation in Kent in August 2024, the bird represents an identity adopted under Malcolm Allison in 1973. Campaigners highlight stressful stadium environment Campaigners highlight stressful stadium environment Campaigners argue that existing costumed characters such as Pete the Eagle are sufficient to entertain the crowd without exposing wildlife to matchday commotion. Their letter stressed that "reclusive eagles deserve better than a stressful, booming stadium environment", warning that "bright lights, loud noises, and boisterous crowds can cause birds to become frightened, disoriented and panicked". Criticising the use of the bird as matchday entertainment, PETA's Dr Carys Bennett said: "Bald eagles are revered as symbols of freedom, yet Phoenix is being used as little more than a prop to entertain football fans. "Crystal Palace already has a human mascot to energise supporters, so there's no reason to drag a wild animal into a noisy, crowded stadium. PETA is urging the club to let Phoenix spread his wings and retire him from matchday duties for good." Previous incidents underline safety risks To support their plea, the organisation pointed to several alarming episodes involving live birds at football grounds over the years. Highlighting past examples where animals came to harm inside stadiums, the PETA letter cited: "an owl who died after being hit by a ball, eagles who crashed into walls or glass windows, and a falcon who landed on a fan's head, sinking his talons into the man's scalp." Recalling a separate altercation involving an opposing supporter, PETA continued: "In another case, a rowdy football supporter punched a rival team's eagle mascot." That remark refers to an attack on Phoenix's predecessor, Kayla, during a tempestuous League Cup tie against south London rivals Charlton in September 2015. Having regularly flown the length of the pitch following her introduction in 2010, the club's original American bald eagle died of a heart attack in June 2020 aged 28. Mounting pressure precedes Turkish trip Mounting pressure precedes Turkish trip The off-field appeal arrives with manager Pierre Sage already facing scrutiny after collecting just seven points from his side's opening seven league outings. Matters worsened on Sunday when the south Londoners were thrashed 5-0 by fierce rivals Brighton at the Amex Stadium, a rout highlighted by Diego Gomez scoring from the halfway line . Palace will now attempt to respond when they travel to face Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday.

That would have been doing a disservice to myself and everyone involved.” With a new year and a new role came new excitement for the opportunity Davis had earned. item.title: Nick Nurse still thinks 76ers ‘should have won’ vs. Knicks in 2026 playoffs
item.description: Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Nick Nurse still thinks 76ers ‘should have won’ vs. Knicks in 2026 playoffs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . They say that having the memory of a goldfish is helpful when it comes to professional sports. Forgetting about losses and focusing on what’s ahead is important to keeping an even-keeled demeanor. But there are some who thrive off of remembering, and Philadelphia 76ers head coach Nick Nurse certainly seems to be one of those people. On Tuesday night, the 76ers spoiled the New York Knicks’ ring and banner ceremony, handing them a 106-100 loss at Madison Square Garden. For Nurse, this victory must have felt satisfying, especially when he still feels that Philly should have won during their previous trip to the Garden for Game 2 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. “The last time we were here, we should’ve won. Still makes me mad,” Nurse said after the game, per Jeff Skversky of FOX29 Philly. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The last time we were here, we should've won. Still makes me mad” 🔥 Nick Nurse after the Sixers beat the Knicks in the opener with LeBron James and new look 76ers Nurse says it’s been “fun” so far with this team pic.twitter.com/vXjz9dDKPf — Jeff Skversky (@JeffSkversky) October 21, 2026 The 76ers were coming off a 137-98 loss in Game 1 of that series, and to make matters worse, Joel Embiid had to miss Game 2. Despite Embiid’s absence, Philly took a 90-89 lead into the fourth quarter of Game 2, putting forth a brilliant effort in their quest to even up the series heading back home. Alas, the 76ers ran cold in the fourth . They scored just 12 points as the team shot just 4-of-19 from the field, and the Knicks, as would be the case for the entirety of their championship run, completed the come-from-behind victory. Philly would go on to lose Game 3 and Game 4 at home in convincing fashion as the Knicks swept them. That is the sort of loss that sticks with anyone, especially with a cerebral head coach like Nurse. But now, the 76ers should have the tools to weather whatever kind of adversity that hits them. With the arrival of Jaylen Brown and LeBron James, they have stars other than Tyrese Maxey who can soak up huge offensive responsibilities just in case the injury bug hits Embiid once again at the most inopportune moment. The 76ers showed on Opening Night that they can win even without shooting the ball very well, and this bodes well for their chances of being one of the best teams in the East moving forward. item.title: Here's what Joey Votto thought of Caminero's 38-second home run trot
item.description: Former Cincinnati Reds great Joey Votto was asked during MLB Network's "MLB Now" whether he thinks there should be limits to the amount a player celebrates a home run after Junior Caminero's 38.66-second homer trot during the seventh inning of the Tampa Bay Rays ' ALCS-clinching 7-3 win against the Cleveland Guardians . "No, he's got me smiling," Votto said. "I'm so excited for that for that moment because (it's a) game-changing, season-changing moment. Pedro Martinez tweeted something along the lines of 'this is the way we play.'You know, they're both Dominican baseball players. 'This is the way we play. We show our passion.We show our enthusiasm for the sports, for our country, for everything that we've come from in these particular moments.'" "I saw a young man who's about to go to the World Series, and really, he was just a kid," Votto continued. "And if you're at home, and … you're tuning into your Tampa Bay Rays, about to go to the World Series, you're in your living room, pumping your fists, jumping up and down, dancing with your kids." "And Caminero is doing that on the field with you," Votto added. "And I think that it's just a beautiful thing. I understand back in the day, you put your head down and you try (to) act like you've done it before. We're not there anymore. And I think, especially in that particular moment, because Caminero, when you hit 40, 50 home runs, you're experienced. But he's not doing this on a consistent basis during the regular season. He's doing this in this one particular moment. I loved it." After Chris "Mad Dog" Russo explained that he thought Caminero's celebration was excessive, Votto disagreed with him. "I, Caminero and players that are in the box on a consistent basis, getting balls fired at us under our chin, over our head," Votto replied. "What do we owe to the average pitcher? Truly. Yandy Diaz got hit yesterday. What do we owe to you? We owe you nothing. And you know what, when we get you in a big moment, we're going to dunk on you and celebrate. And that's what I saw from Caminero." Votto recently told Foul Territory he believes there's an "underinvestment in the easy wins" from the Reds. In the same interview, Votto was asked what his top priority would be as general manager of the team . "I would trade Elly for as many prospects as possible to start," Votto said . Votto shared earlier in the month that he got to see the clock he gave as a gift earlier in the year, during a visit to Crosley Terrace, outside the main entrance of Great American Ball Park. In September, Votto replied to National Baseball Hall of Famer and Reds analyst Barry Larkin 's rant that followed a loss to Chicago by tweeting, "Captain Lark 100 (emoji)." item.title: Former Bills Pro Bowl WR Signs With Colts Day After Firing GM Chris Ballard
item.description: ROCHESTER, NEW YORK - JULY 29: Mecole Hardman Jr. #1 of the Buffalo Bills runs sprints during training camp at St. John Fisher University on July 29, 2026 in Rochester, New York. (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) Getty Former Buffalo Bills wide receiver Mecole Hardman Jr. has found a new home. The Indianapolis Colts signed Hardman to their practice squad on Tuesday. Hardman appeared in two games for the Bills last season but caught no passes. The 28-year-old wide receiver was on the Buffalo training camp roster, but he did not make the 53-man active roster after the preseason. Many NFL fans probably remember Hardman from his time with the Kansas City Chiefs, where he spent six seasons in two stints. He spent 2019 to 2023 with the Chiefs before signing with the New York Jets. However, he returned to the Chiefs midseason and stayed through the rest of that season and into 2024. Hardman caught 1,77 receptions for 2,296 yards and 16 touchdowns in 75 games with the Chiefs, helped win three Super Bowls, and made the 2019 Pro Bowl. Hardman Caught a Game-Winning Super Bowl Pass The Chiefs couldn’t have won Super Bowl LVII without Hardman. Kansas City beat the San Francisco 49ers in that Super Bowl because Patrick Mahomes found Hardman on a 3-yard touchdown pass in overtime, giving Mahomes his third Super Bowl ring. But Hardman didn’t realize his touchdown reception won the Super Bowl for the Chiefs. “I blacked out, man,” Hardman said after making the catch, via Fox Sports. “I forgot we actually won the game.” “I threw a touchdown to this dude to end the game, and he looked at me,” Mahomes said. “He had no idea. I said, ‘Dude, we just won the Super Bowl.’ He had no idea. He didn’t even celebrate at the beginning.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Former Bills Pro Bowl WR Signs With Colts Day After Firing GM Chris Ballard appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: ‘I’ve Heard Forever That Peyton Manning Has an Interest’ – Insider Checks the Temperature on Rumors Linking NFL Legend With GM Role in Indianapolis
item.description: Peyton Manning prepares to give a speech during Jim Irsay's Ring of Honor induction on Sunday, Sept. 7, 2025, during the game at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. The Colts have a bigger question to answer than who replaces Chris Ballard. After 10 years with Ballard running football operations, Indianapolis has a chance to rethink who makes the biggest decisions and how much influence the next hire will have. That has also put a familiar name into the conversation: Peyton Manning. But would the franchise’s legendary former quarterback actually consider stepping into an NFL front office, or would the Colts be better off simply asking him for advice? Albert Breer Raises Peyton Manning Question After Colts Fire Chris Ballard Speaking on the “10.19 Pod,” Breer suggested Indianapolis could use Ballard’s departure to reconsider its entire organizational structure, including whether Peyton Manning could have a role in the franchise’s future. “The Colts have fired their general manager, Chris Ballard, after a loss to the Titans. This, to me, opens the opportunity for them to look at, do we reimagine the organization?” Breer said. He pointed to the Atlanta Falcons, who brought in consultants during the previous season, as an example of a team evaluating its leadership before the year ended. Conor Orr responded, “Here come the consultants.” Breer then explained how a midseason front-office change could affect Indianapolis beyond its executive suite. “That means, going forward, the entire roster, no one can feel great about their place in Indianapolis going forward,” he said. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor The uncertainty could also extend to coach Shane Steichen. Co-host Conor Orr believes the head coach might become collateral damage as the franchise reassesses its leadership. He noted that coaches have long felt general managers receive greater protection because of their relationship with ownership. This possibility brings Manning into the conversation. The Colts icon remains closely associated with the franchise, and Breer believes Indianapolis could at least explore his interest in a leadership position. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator “Do they call Peyton Manning? I’ve heard forever that Peyton Manning has an interest, and eventually, he’s going to have an interest in running a team,” Breer said. “I wonder if that’s the first phone call you make now.” Breer added that Manning could offer valuable advice even if he does not pursue the job. “At the very least, to get his insight because, you know, he knows everyone,” he said. Manning has not held a traditional NFL front-office position, and taking the job would mean weighing its demands against his work with Omaha Productions and ESPN’s ManningCast. Indianapolis previously approached him about a leadership role before the 2017 season, but he declined. As things stand, Breer’s comments raise a possibility rather than confirm a hiring plan.

item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
